words: لا جناح عليهن في آبائهن ولا أبنائهن
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Women incur no sin by leaving the veil before the listed relatives.
rows.anchor: لا إثم عليهن في ترك الاحتجاب من هؤلاء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view takes “their women” to mean Muslim women, so Jewish and Christian women may not enter among them.
rows.anchor: قيل: أراد به النساء المسلمات، حتى لا يجوز للكتابيات

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view includes Muslim and non-Muslim women; they are called their women because they share their kind.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو عام في المسلمات والكتابيات، وإنما قال: "ولا نسائهن"

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some hold that a woman's male slave is a mahram, based on the phrase “those whom their right hands possess.”
rows.anchor: فقال قوم يكون محرما لقوله عز وجل: "ولا ما ملكت أيمانهن"

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Others treat a woman's male slave like unrelated men and read the verse as referring to female slaves only.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: هو كالأجانب، والمراد من الآية الإماء دون العبيد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The women are to fear God lest someone outside the listed relations see them; God witnesses every deed.
rows.anchor: {واتقين الله} أن يراكن غير هؤلاء، {إن الله كان على كل شيء}

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains God's prayer as mercy for the Prophet and the angels' prayer as supplication for him.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: أراد إن الله يرحم النبي، والملائكة يدعون له.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is also reported to explain “they pray” as seeking blessing.
rows.anchor: وعن ابن عباس أيضا: "يصلون" يتبركون.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation says God's prayer is mercy and the angels' prayer is seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الصلاة من الله: الرحمة، ومن الملائكة: الاستغفار.

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abu al-Aliyah says God's prayer is praise of the Prophet before the angels, while the angels pray for him.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو العالية: صلاة الله: ثناؤه عليه عند الملائكة، وصلاة الملائكة: الدعاء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are to ask God for mercy upon the Prophet and greet him with the greeting of Islam.
rows.anchor: أي: ادعوا له بالرحمة، {وسلموا تسليما} أي: حيوه بتحية الإسلام.

rows.speaker: كعب بن عجرة
rows.claim: Kaʿb reports that the Prophet taught them a formula asking blessings on Muhammad and his family as on Abraham and his family.
rows.anchor: لقيني كعب بن عجرة فقال: ألا أهدي لك هدية سمعتها من النبي

rows.speaker: أبو حميد الساعي
rows.claim: Abu Humayd reports that the Prophet taught a formula invoking blessing on Muhammad, his wives, and descendants as on Abraham's family.
rows.anchor: أخبرني أبو حميد الساعي أنهم قالوا: يا رسول الله كيف نصلي عليك؟ فقال رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The provision from heaven is rain, and the provision from earth is vegetation; if the questioners do not name God, Muhammad is to answer that God provides for them.
rows.anchor: فالرزق من السموات: المطر، ومن الأرض: النبات، {قل الله} أي:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is fair argument, not doubt: like saying “one of us is lying” while knowing oneself truthful, it conveys that one side is guided and the other astray without an explicit accusation.
rows.anchor: ليس هذا على طريق الشك ولكن على جهة الإنصاف في الحجاج

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some take “or” as “and” and the alif as extra, yielding the sense that the Muslims are guided and their opponents astray.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: "أو" بمعنى الواو، والألف فيه صلة، كأنه قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gathers the disputing parties on the Day of Resurrection and judges between them justly; al-Fattah means the Judge.
rows.anchor: يعني: يوم القيامة، {ثم يفتح} يقضي، {بيننا بالحق وهو الفتاح العليم}

words: قُلْ أَرُونِىَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَلْحَقْتُم بِهِۦ شُرَكَآءَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks them to identify their alleged partners and whether they can create or provide; they cannot, so God alone is mighty and wise, with no partner in His dominion.
rows.anchor: أي: أعلموني الذين ألحقتموهم به، أي: بالله، شركاء في العبادة معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is dominant in His affairs and wise in governing creation, so He cannot have a partner in His kingdom.
rows.anchor: الغالب على أمره، {الحكيم} في تدبيره لخلقه فأنى يكون له شريك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet was sent to all people, red and black, as bearer of good news and warning.
rows.anchor: يعني: للناس عامة أحمرهم وأسودهم، {بشيرا ونذيرا} أي: مبشرا ومنذرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Those you invoke apart from Him” refers to idols.
rows.anchor: والذين تدعون من دونه} يعني: الأصنام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A qitmir is the thin film covering a date stone.
rows.anchor: ما يملكون من قطمير} وهو لفافة النواة، وهي القشرة الرقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idols do not hear their invocations, and even if they heard, they would not answer them.
rows.anchor: يعني: إن تدعو الأصنام، {لا يسمعوا دعاءكم ولو سمعوا ما استجابوا لكم}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Resurrection the idols will disown their worshippers and their worship, saying that the worshippers did not worship them.
rows.anchor: يتبرؤون منكم ومن عبادتكم إياها، يقولون: ما كنتم إيانا تعبدون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “all-knowing expert” is God Himself; no one can inform the Prophet as one who knows all things does.
rows.anchor: يعني: نفسه أي: لا ينبئك أحد مثلي خبير عالم بالأشياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People are needy for God's favor; a faqir is one who is in need.
rows.anchor: إلى فضل الله والفقير المحتاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has no need of His creation and is praised for His beneficence toward them.
rows.anchor: الغني عن خلقه المحمود في إحسانه إليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can remove people and bring a new creation; doing so is no difficulty for Him.
rows.anchor: وما ذلك على الله بعزيز} شديد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No soul bearing sin can carry another soul's burden.
rows.anchor: ولا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A “burdened” person is weighed down by sins; the burden is the sins she carries, and no one summoned can bear any of it, even a close relative.
rows.anchor: أي: نفس مثقلة بذنوبها غيرها، {إلى حملها} أي: حمل ما عليه من الذنوب، {لا يحمل منه شيء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas describes a father or mother asking a child to carry some of their sins, while the child replies that he cannot and must answer for his own burden.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يلقى الأب والأم ابنه فيقول: يا بني احمل عني بعض ذنوبي.

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb names the first two messengers John and Paul.
rows.anchor: قال وهب: اسمهما يوحنا وبولس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means that God strengthened the two messengers with a third.
rows.anchor: {فكذبوهما فعززنا} يعني: فقوينا، {بثالث} برسول ثالث،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third messenger was Simon.
rows.anchor: {بثالث} برسول ثالث، وهو شمعون،

rows.speaker: أبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: Abu Bakr's transmission from Asim reads the verb without doubling the z; it has the same sense as the doubled form, like lightened and doubled forms of “strengthened.”
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو بكر عن عاصم: "فعززنا" بالتخفيف وهو بمعنى الأول كقولك: شددنا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes the verb to mean “we overcame,” from the saying “whoever prevails takes it.”
rows.anchor: وقيل: أي: فغلبنا من قولهم: من عز بز.

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb names the first two messengers Sadiq and Sadduq and the third Shalum; God attributes their dispatch to Himself because Jesus sent them by God's command.
rows.anchor: وقال كعب: الرسولان: صادق وصدوق، والثالث شلوم، وإنما أضاف الله الإرسال إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All three messengers address the people of Antioch and declare that they were sent to them.
rows.anchor: {فقالوا} جميعا لأهل أنطاكية، {إنا إليكم مرسلون} .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople accuse the messengers of lying about their claim to be sent.
rows.anchor: ما أنتم إلا كاذبون فيما تزعمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople took the messengers as an ill omen because the rain had stopped, and blamed them for it.
rows.anchor: تشاءمنا بكم، وذلك أن المطر حبس عنهم، فقالوا: أصابنا هذا بشؤمكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their threat to stone the messengers means they would kill them.
rows.anchor: لنقتلنكم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada specifically explains the threatened stoning as throwing stones at them.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: بالحجارة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The townspeople threaten to inflict painful punishment on the messengers.
rows.anchor: وليمسنكم منا عذاب أليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers say the townspeople's misfortune comes from their own disbelief and denial, not from the messengers.
rows.anchor: يعني: شؤمكم معكم بكفركم وتكذيبكم يعني: أصابكم الشؤم من قبلكم.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas and al-Dahhak take “your omen” to mean your share of good and evil.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس 92/أوالضحاك: حظكم من الخير والشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means “if you are admonished about God”; its interrogative has an omitted response, with the sense that they react to admonition by taking the messengers as an omen.
rows.anchor: يعني: وعظتم بالله، وهذا استفهام محذوف الجواب مجازه: إن ذكرتم

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar reads the hamza with fatḥa and softens the hamza, and reads “dhukkirtum” without doubling.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر: "أن" بفتح الهمزة الملينة "ذكرتم" بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people are polytheists who have exceeded the proper bounds.
rows.anchor: {بل أنتم قوم مسرفون} مشركون مجاوزون الحد.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man who came running from the far end of the city was Habib al-Najjar.
rows.anchor: وهو حبيب النجار

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Habib al-Najjar was a fuller.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: كان قصارا

rows.speaker: وهب
rows.claim: Wahb says Habib al-Najjar worked with silk.
rows.anchor: وقال وهب: كان رجلا يعمل الحرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Habib was a believer with advanced leprosy who lived by the city's farthest gate; each evening he divided his earnings between his family and charity, and came when he heard the messengers were in danger.
rows.anchor: وكان سقيما قد أسرع فيه الجذام، وكان منزله عند أقصى باب من أبواب المدينة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The livestock provide wool, fur, hair, offspring, and milk, blessings for which people should thank their Lord.
rows.anchor: منافع} من أصوافها وأوبارها وأشعارها ونسلها {ومشارب} من ألبانها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters took gods besides God hoping they would protect them from God's punishment, but that will never happen.
rows.anchor: يعني: لتمنعهم من عذاب الله، ولا يكون ذلك قط.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says idols cannot help their worshippers or keep them from punishment.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لا تقدر الأصنام على نصرهم ومنعهم من العذاب.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In this life the idolaters are troops for their idols, defending and attending them, though the idols bring no good and cannot help them.
rows.anchor: أي: الكفار جند للأصنام يغضبون لها ويحضرونها في الدنيا، وهي لا تسوق إليهم خيرا،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view places this in the afterlife: each idol and its worshippers will be brought together as a troop in Hell.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هذا في الآخرة، يؤتى بكل معبود من دون الله تعالى ومعه أتباعه الذين عبدوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The words that should not grieve Muhammad are the Meccan disbelievers' statements denying him.
rows.anchor: يعني: قول كفار مكة في تكذيبك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows their inward denial and what they make public, whether worship of idols or hurtful words.
rows.anchor: في ضمائرهم من التكذيب {وما يعلنون} من عبادة الأصنام أو ما يعلنون بألسنتهم من الأذى.

words: أَوَلَمْ يَرَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ أَنَّا خَلَقْنَٰهُ مِن نُّطْفَةٍ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The human is made from a drop, yet becomes an obvious contentious disputant; he should reflect on his beginning and stop arguing against resurrection.
rows.anchor: أنه مخلوق من نطفة ثم يخاصم فكيف لا يتفكر في بدء خلقه حتى يدع الخصومة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who challenged the Prophet with a decayed bone and asked whether God would revive it; the Prophet answered yes, saying Ubayy would also be raised and enter Hell.
rows.anchor: نزلت في أبي بن خلف الجمحي خاصم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في إنكار البعث، وأتاه بعظم قد بلي ففتته بيده،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “He forgot his creation” means that he forgot how his own origin began.
rows.anchor: نسي خلقه} بدء أمره، ثم {قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم} بالية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ramim means worn and decayed; the form is used instead of feminine ramimah because it is diverted from its usual feminine pattern.
rows.anchor: {قال من يحيي العظام وهي رميم} بالية، ولم يقل رميمة؛ لأنه معدول عن فاعلة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Forms diverted from their usual form do not follow their ordinary counterparts; Maryam 19:28 similarly has baghiy without the feminine ending because it is diverted from baghiyah.
rows.anchor: عن وجهه ووزنه كان مصروفا عن أخواته (1) ، كقوله: "وما كانت أمك بغيا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The One who first brought the bones into being is the One who will revive them; “created” explains “brought into being.”
rows.anchor: {قل يحييها الذي أنشأها} خلقها (2) ، {أول مرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every created thing.
rows.anchor: وهو بكل خلق عليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who were astonished are the disbelievers mentioned earlier; they objected that a warner and messenger came from among themselves and called him a lying magician.
rows.anchor: يعني: الكفار الذين ذكرهم الله عز وجل في قوله: "بل الذين كفروا"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Umar embraced Islam, Quraysh's leaders sought Abu Talib's mediation, asking Muhammad to stop denouncing their idols; he offered them the declaration of God's oneness, which they rejected as one God could not suffice all creation.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أسلم، فشق ذلك على قريش، وفرح به المؤمنون،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah convened twenty-five Quraysh notables, the eldest being himself; Muhammad offered a single phrase that would make Arabs and non-Arabs obey them, and Abu Jahl promised ten times as much before they recoiled from “There is no god but God.”
rows.anchor: وكانوا خمسة وعشرين رجلا أكبرهم سنا الوليد بن المغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The leaders left the gathering at Abu Talib's and told one another to go and remain steadfast in worship of their gods.
rows.anchor: أي: انطلقوا من مجلسهم الذي كانوا فيه عند أبي طالب، يقول بعضهم لبعض: امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Be patient over your gods” means to persist in worshipping them.
rows.anchor: أي: اثبتوا على عبادة آلهتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They viewed the Muslims' growing numbers after Umar's conversion as a deliberate plan against them, since his standing strengthened the Muslims.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن عمر لما أسلم وحصل للمسلمين قوة بمكانه قالوا: إن هذا الذي نراه من زيادة أصحاب محمد

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other explanations are that the plan is intended for the people of earth, or that Muhammad intends to rule over them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: يراد بأهل الأرض، وقيل: يراد بمحمد أن يملك علينا.

words: مَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِى ٱلْمِلَّةِ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, al-Kalbi, and Muqatil say “the last religion” means Christianity, the latest religion, whose adherents do not affirm unity but say “three of three.”
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما، والكلبي، ومقاتل: يعنون النصرانية، لأنها آخر الملل وهم لا يوحدون،

words: مَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَٰذَا فِى ٱلْمِلَّةِ ٱلْءَاخِرَةِ
rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid and Qatada instead say it refers to the Quraysh religion and the faith they follow.
rows.anchor: وقال مجاهد وقتادة: يعنون ملة قريش ودينهم الذي هم عليه.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ikhtilaq means a lie and fabrication.
rows.anchor: {إن هذا إلا اختلاق} كذب وافتعال.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccans objected that the Quran was sent down to Muhammad rather than to someone older or more noble among them.
rows.anchor: القرآن {من بيننا} وليس بأكبرنا ولا أشرفنا، يقوله أهل مكة.

words: بَلْ هُم فِى شَكٍّ مِّن ذِكْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They doubt God's revelation, and have not yet tasted punishment; if they had, they would not have made this claim.
rows.anchor: أي وحيي وما أنزلت، {بل لما يذوقوا عذاب} ولو ذاقوه لما قالوا هذا القول.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks whether they possess the keys of God's favor, meaning the keys of prophethood to give to whomever they choose; see 43:32.
rows.anchor: أي: نعمة ربك يعني: مفاتيح النبوة يعطونها من شاؤوا، نظيره:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is mighty in His dominion and the giver who bestowed prophethood on Muhammad.
rows.anchor: [العزيز في ملكه، الوهاب] (1) وهب النبوة لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water is made to flow underground as springs and wells.
rows.anchor: ماء فسلكه} أدخل ذلك الماء، {ينابيع} عيونا وركايا

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbi says every bit of water in the earth came down from the sky.
rows.anchor: قال الشعبي: كل ماء في الأرض فمن السماء نزل، {ثم يخرج به}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Water produces crops of different colors, including red, yellow, and green; they dry, turn yellow, and break into fragments, reminding people of understanding.
rows.anchor: {ثم يخرج به} أي: بالماء {زرعا مختلفا ألوانه} أحمر وأصفر وأخضر، {ثم يهيج} ييبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expands the person's breast to accept the truth; being on light from God is unlike having a hardened heart.
rows.anchor: وسعه لقبول الحق، {فهو على نور من ربه} ليس كمن أقسى الله قلبه.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud reports that the Prophet said light entering the heart makes it expand; its signs are turning toward the eternal home, shunning the deceptive home, and preparing for death before it arrives.
rows.anchor: عن عبد الله بن مسعود قال: تلا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: (أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام فهو على نور من ربه)

rows.speaker: مالك بن دينار
rows.claim: Malik ibn Dinar says no punishment inflicted on a servant is worse than a hard heart, and God has never been angry with a people without removing mercy from them.
rows.anchor: قال مالك بن دينار: ما ضرب عبد بعقوبة أعظم من قسوة قلب،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's parts resemble one another in excellence and confirm one another, without contradiction or discrepancy.
rows.anchor: يشبه بعضه بعضا في الحسن، ويصدق بعضه بعضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathani means that the Quran repeats paired themes: promise and threat, command and prohibition, narratives and rulings.
rows.anchor: {مثاني} يثنى فيه ذكر الوعد والوعيد، والأمر والنهي، والأخبار والأحكام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taqshaʿir means to tremble and recoil; gooseflesh is a bodily change brought on by dread and fear.
rows.anchor: {تقشعر} تضطرب وتشمئز، {منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم} والاقشعرار تغير في جلد الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes the skins of those who fear their Lord shuddering.
rows.anchor: منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation takes “skins” to mean the hearts of those who fear their Lord.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المراد من الجلود القلوب، أي: قلوب الذين يخشون ربهم،

words: ثُمَّ تَلِينُ جُلُودُهُمْ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ إِلَىٰ ذِكْرِ ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The skins and hearts soften because of God's remembrance: punishment verses make the fearful shudder, while mercy verses soothe them; their hearts tremble in fear and soften in hope.
rows.anchor: أي: لذكر الله، أي: إذا ذكرت آيات العذاب اقشعرت جلود الخائفين لله، وإذا ذكرت آيات الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The soothing effect of remembrance is linked to the statement that hearts find rest in God's remembrance.
rows.anchor: كما قال الله تعالى: "ألا بذكر الله تطمئن القلوب" (الرعد-28) .

rows.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
rows.claim: Al-Abbas reports that the Prophet said a servant's skin shuddering from fear of God causes sins to fall away like leaves from a dry tree.
rows.anchor: عن العباس بن عبد المطلب قال: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: "إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله تحاتت عنه ذنوبه

rows.speaker: العباس بن عبد المطلب
rows.claim: A second report from al-Abbas says the Prophet stated that God will forbid the Fire to a servant whose skin shudders from fear of Him.
rows.anchor: وقال: "إذا اقشعر جلد العبد من خشية الله حرمه الله على النار"

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says this describes God's friends, whose skins shudder and hearts settle through remembrance; losing reason and fainting are traits of innovators and from Satan.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: هذا نعت أولياء الله نعتهم الله بأن تقشعر جلودهم وتطمئن قلوبهم بذكر الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “That” refers to the best discourse, the Quran.
rows.anchor: {ذلك} يعني: أحسن الحديث،

words: هُدَى ٱللَّهِ يَهْدِى بِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is God's guidance by which He guides whomever He wills; whoever God leads astray has no guide.
rows.anchor: هدى الله يهدي به من يشاء ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The “evil” of punishment means its severity.
rows.anchor: سوء العذاب} أي: شدته، {يوم القيامة}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the condemned person is dragged face first through Hell.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: يجر على وجهه في النار. وقال عطاء:

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says the person is thrown into Hell upside down, so the face is the first part touched by the fire.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: يرمى به في النار منكوسا فأول شيء منه تمسه النار وجهه. قال مقاتل:

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil describes the unbeliever bound with his hands to his neck and a huge sulfur rock at his neck; its fire and heat strike his face, which the bonds prevent him from shielding.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: هو أن الكافر يرمى به في النار مغلولة يداه إلى عنقه، وفي عنقه صخرة مثل جبل عظيم من الكبريت،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's implied comparison asks whether one guarding his face from punishment can be like someone safe from punishment.
rows.anchor: ومجاز الآية: أفمن يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب كمن هو آمن من العذاب؟

words: وَقِيلَ لِلظَّٰلِمِينَ ذُوقُوا۟ مَا كُنتُمْ تَكْسِبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ones saying “taste what you earned” are the keepers of Hell; what the wrongdoers taste is the consequence of their deeds.
rows.anchor: {وقيل} يعني: تقول الخزنة، {للظالمين ذوقوا ما كنتم تكسبون} أي: وباله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People before the Meccan unbelievers denied the messengers, and punishment came upon them unexpectedly while they were heedless and secure.
rows.anchor: {كذب الذين من قبلهم} من قبل كفار مكة كذبوا الرسل، {فأتاهم العذاب من حيث لا يشعرون} يعني: وهم آمنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made them taste humiliation, meaning punishment and disgrace in worldly life; the punishment of the next life is greater.
rows.anchor: {فأذاقهم الله الخزي} العذاب والهوان، {في الحياة الدنيا ولعذاب الآخرة أكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives people every kind of parable in the Quran so that they may take heed.
rows.anchor: {ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل لعلهم يتذكرون} يتعظون.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “An Arabic Quran” is in the accusative as a circumstantial expression.
rows.anchor: {قرآنا عربيا} نصب على الحال،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “not crooked” as not differing.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: غير مختلف.

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid explains “not crooked” as free of ambiguity.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: غير ذي لبس.

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi explains the phrase as meaning that the Quran is not created; the same is transmitted from Malik ibn Anas.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: غير مخلوق. ويروى ذلك عن مالك بن أنس،

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah relates that seventy Successors held that the Quran is neither creator nor created.
rows.anchor: وحكي عن سفيان بن عيينة عن سبعين من التابعين أن القرآن ليس بخالق ولا مخلوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran is intended to help people guard against disbelief and denial of it.
rows.anchor: {لعلهم يتقون} الكفر والتكذيب به.

words: فَمَنْ أَظْلَمُ مِمَّن كَذَبَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who lies about God is claiming that He has a child and a partner; the truth they deny is the Quran.
rows.anchor: فزعم أن له ولدا وشريكا، {وكذب بالصدق} بالقرآن،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathwa means a dwelling or place of residence, and the question is stated as an assertion.
rows.anchor: {إذ جاءه أليس في جهنم مثوى} منزل ومقام، {للكافرين} استفهام بمعنى التقرير.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says Muhammad brought the truth, “There is no god but God,” and the Messenger also affirmed it by conveying it to creation.
rows.anchor: 106/ب قال ابن عباس: "والذي جاء بالصدق" يعني رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم جاء بلا إله إلا الله "وصدق به"

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Gabriel brought the Quran and Muhammad affirmed it by receiving it with acceptance.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: "والذي جاء بالصدق" جبريل جاء بالقرآن، "وصدق به" محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: الكلبي وأبو العالية
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi and Abu al-Aliyah say Muhammad brought the truth and Abu Bakr affirmed it.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي وأبو العالية: "والذي جاء بالصدق" رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "وصدق به" أبو بكر

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل
rows.claim: Qatada and Muqatil say Muhammad brought the truth and the believers affirmed it, as indicated by the following description of them as God-fearing.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة ومقاتل: "والذي جاء بالصدق" رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم "وصدق به" هم المؤمنون،

rows.speaker: عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says the prophets brought the truth and their followers affirmed it; here the singular “one who” has a plural sense, as in 2:17.
rows.anchor: وقال عطاء: "والذي جاء بالصدق" الأنبياء "وصدق به" الأتباع، وحينئذ يكون الذي بمعنى: الذين،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says the believers affirmed the truth in this life and will bring it with them in the next.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: هم المؤمنون صدقوا به في الدنيا وجاءوا به في الآخرة.

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masud's reading makes both expressions plural: “those who brought the truth and affirmed it.”
rows.anchor: وفي قراءة عبد الله بن مسعود: والذين جاءوا بالصدق وصدقوا به.

words: لِيُكَفِّرَ ٱللَّهُ عَنْهُمْ أَسْوَأَ ٱلَّذِى عَمِلُوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God covers their worst deeds by forgiving them.
rows.anchor: يسترها عليهم بالمغفرة، {ويجزيهم أجرهم

words: وَيَجْزِيَهُمْ أَجْرَهُم بِأَحْسَنِ ٱلَّذِى كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ
rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil says God rewards them for their good deeds and does not repay them for their bad deeds.
rows.anchor: قال مقاتل: يجزيهم بالمحاسن من أعمالهم ولا يجزيهم بالمساوئ.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular “His servant” refers to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: يعني: محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم،

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, Hamzah, and al-Kisaʾi read “His servants” in the plural, referring to the prophets whom their peoples targeted with harm; God protected them, as in 40:5.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وحمزة والكسائي: "عباده" بالجمع يعني: الأنبياء عليهم السلام، قصدهم قومهم بالسوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters threatened Muhammad with harm from their idols if he did not stop insulting their gods, including derangement or madness.
rows.anchor: وذلك أنهم خوفوا النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم معرة الأوثان. وقالوا: لتكفن عن شتم آلهتنا

words: وَمَن يُضْلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُۥ مِنْ هَادٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whomever God leads astray has no guide.
rows.anchor: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد
